items.text: People's Square, Rayashki
People stream in from all directions.
They stand now at the crossroads of the town's fate.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: *clears throat* People of Rayashki, my dear friends, good day to you all.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Over the past two days, Zeno has assessed the potential risks and benefits in the area, and held hearings on what should be done about the future of this town.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Our hearings saw very limited attendance. We've taken that to be a gesture of approval.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Mr. Evgeni has put in a great effort helping to make these changes happen. We all owe him a great deal. Thank you, sir.
He motions to Evgeni at his side.
A freshly printed document unfurls before all present, Zeno's seal stamped deliberately in the most prominent position.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Please believe that we have made the best decision we could for you.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We all know the runium here has run dry, and the land has been exhausted of all further material wealth, now and into the foreseeable future.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: As a result, your local processing factory has lost its intended purpose.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: What's more, Zeno has changed our cooperation strategy. Though your town's loyalty will never be forgotten, we must have a sober-minded view of its costs and benefits.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: To sum up, our final decision is that ...

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We will be ending operations and all future cooperation between Zeno and Rayashki.
A heavy hammer swings in the square, producing a whistling wind.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Well, Mr. Bertolt, you have just got here; perhaps you didn't have enough time to get to know us well enough. Rayashki's value is not just in our runium. We have many other factories, too.
Urgent words of protest flood in from all sides.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Yes, you have a brick factory, a power plant, many forklifts, a smattering of conveyor belts. But all these were all built and suited for only the processing of runium ore.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Without the ore, they simply have no benefit to us.
The crowd murmurs, voices bubbling up and simmering like boiling water.
Bertolt raps the table, ending the broil.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Now that you have full knowledge of the situation and our intentions, we want to assure you that your loyalty has not been forgotten, so we have generously prepared two choices for the future of Rayashki.
The assembly hushes.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Firstly, Zeno believes that you have many valuable qualities. The determination and skills you've shown in the past year of our cooperation have proved that your people can be a great asset to us.
Bertolt scans across the faces looking back at him.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Indeed, many of you already meet the entrance requirements to join Zeno.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Therefore, on behalf of Zeno Arms Academy, I wish to extend a heartfelt invitation to you.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Leave Rayashki. Join us and work for one of our other branches as members of Zeno.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: What are you saying!? You want us to abandon our home for some promise of a job?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Calm down, Mr. Knut. This is not about abandoning your home. It's about joining us in our efforts to contribute to world peace. Through a more optimized allocation of manpower.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: So you're just going to pack us all up and ship us away to work for Zeno?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You misunderstand, madam.
He closes the folder, looking conspicuously towards the children beside Windsong.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Every year, Zeno dismisses 4% of our employees because they failed to pass our rigorous work reviews. And the number of our colleagues that are killed in the line of duty is even larger still.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Working for Zeno is a privilege, not a gift.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: That's why only a small number of you will be allowed to come and work for us.

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Now, according to Article 58 in the section on "protection of arcanist rights" signed at the Event Horizon Convention ...

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We will provide basic supplies for any residents who haven't been offered a position with Zeno. They will be transferred immediately to the nearest relief station until our social workers contact them for further arrangements.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: So then, you're suggesting you will send our children and elderly away to some kind of refugee station?

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: And the rest of us must go to work for Zeno without any questions?

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: You ****! This is total rubbish!
He waves off, then pushes aside the Zeno soldier in front of him.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Sir, please lower your voice.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Well. You would be glad to know that your work experience in particular is valuable to Zeno, Mr. Knut.
He attempts a pat on Knut's shoulder, who shrugs him off.
But Bertolt acts entirely unfazed, unfolding the document further.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: If you're not interested in our first plan, we have another.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: If the residents in the area prove reluctant to relocate, Zeno can offer another alternative. As stated earlier, Rayashki is a remote town that possesses some significant industrial infrastructure.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Therefore, it could be considered an ideal location for a new complex of arms factories.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: There would be a need to substantially upgrade the Rayashki wharf. To turn it into one of the seaports Zeno plans to build across the globe.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Additionally, a radio station will be constructed within the town.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Which will better facilitate our communication throughout the Arctic region so as to stabilize and coordinate with other powers in the area.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We will now be passing out forms, listing the options I've presented. Please fill them in with your choice.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: So your only other option is to turn Rayashki into some kind of military base under Zeno's control?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I won't put it so bluntly, but you're not incorrect.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Our resources, as much as anyone's, are limited, and they must be put to good use. We cannot afford to waste them on strategically usele- ... costly people and places.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: If you want Zeno to help you, you should be able to give us something in return, don't you agree?
He folds the proposal again with satisfaction.
The crowd heaves in protest, held at bay by the soldiers around Bertolt.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: So, Evgeni, this is "the best choice" you made for all of us?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Ahem! I must speak in Mr. Evgeni's defense. He is committed to his duty and only wishes to do what he can for his compatriots.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Shameless! All you've done is sold us out!

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: You tell them, Knut!

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Do you think it's getting a bit windy lately? Clearly, with all the hot air in Evgeni's head, his mind has been blown away!
Countless eyes fall on Evgeni. Disappointment, sadness—perhaps something more complex.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I swear to you, I am not doing this out of my own interest.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Comrades, there are many better places in this world, and you have better purposes to fulfill.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: You shouldn't waste your time here.

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Bah!
The bear of a man puffs up with anger.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Let's all calm down, my friends! It's time to be reasonable!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Think carefully. Zeno has been very generous regarding the offers before you.
He readies himself, as if about to launch into a grand prepared speech, but his hand trembles.
A chill wind sweeps over him.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Generous? Now that's ridiculous!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We won't let you take away our family and friends, nor are we about to let you turn our town into a puppet state!

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: We will stay here! No matter what!

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Comrades, I understand how you feel right now.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: But we must face the cruel reality of our situation.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: And you're willing to send away our own people or give up on all we've built here because of this so-called "reality."

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: It is the only way forward.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: If we continue to stay here without any help, it will be the end of us either way.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Do we have to turn to Zeno for this help?
Evgeni fails to react at first, but a defeated expression comes over him.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: The truth is, just as Rayashki's economy has been dependent on runium, we remain dependent on Zeno.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Without them, at the present rate of consumption, we will be out of supplies and materials within a year.
A silent tidal shift sweeps over those assembled.
The researcher observes the change with harsh recognition.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: This situation looks bad.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Zeno is determined to gain control over this place.
She touches the unsealed letter. Her fingers jump away, as if it had been electrified.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But if I complete the task as Zeno requested, does it mean ...
Bertolt's words echo in her ears.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I will shatter their dream?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: And what about my dream?
The words stick in her throat.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Did the people who refused to acknowledge the study of ley lines act out of the same self-interest?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I've seen this happen so many times before.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: A simple dream is made to face a cruel reality. Where the clever ones give up and leave, and the stubborn fools remain, waiting to be crushed.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: "We asked for our misery."
She turns, her mixed feelings refusing to settle.
The wall of soldiers has suppressed most of the dissent in the square.
But still, some bravely charge forward.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Wait!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'm not finished.
Bertolt dismisses her with his hand as he leaves the stage.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: But I am, Ms. Vila.
The researcher remains stunned, but this potent chemistry of hope and resolve begins to catalyze something in her.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Sir! With all due respect. I can't complete this task alone.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: As an ordinary researcher, I can relate to them. Please forgive me for interrupting.
She lifts her head proudly, looking out in the direction of the crowd.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I have heard so much about Rayashki these days.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: They started from nothing, but bit by bit, they accomplished the impossible.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Their voice should be heard.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Природа это числа и черты.
The soil and snow under her feet becomes imbued with new life, rising up around her.
They clamp onto military boots and surge up and into gun barrels, plugging them up in a comical fashion.
The teacher seizes on this opportunity.
She climbs over the wall of confused soldiers and charges forward.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: Miste- ... Mister Bertolt.

items.speaker: Zeno Soldier
items.text: We can't hold them any longer!
Their conflict ceases.
Scaly palms forcefully grab Bertolt's arm, sharp nails tearing at his sleeve.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Now, will you listen to me?
A clean, new ledger is stuffed into Bertolt's hands.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We don't need your help. Your soldiers and your tyranny are no longer welcome here.
Vila turns around to face her people.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Comrades, what do you say? Shall we solve the problem with the strength of our own hands and hearts?

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: What else can we do? This is what we've always done when there was a problem!

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: There will be more solutions than problems if we work together!

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: If I must die, I will die here with all of you!

items.speaker: Knut
items.text: Just stop talking nonsense, you idiot! Nobody is going to die!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Rayashki belongs to all of us. We will stand with it till its last moment!
The sudden surge of conviction and unity cows the guards as they move backwards.
Many blush with shame.
Some of them quietly withdraw.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Huh, they might say they're just ordinary people, but they are so brave and noble.
